metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most of the author's questions name specific identifiers or decisions in the output: the 'Blob changed' message, store_git, ensure_line, vault_dir_exists, the vault_dir variable, the vault_pass/vault_history split, the temp path and the hardcoded 'vault'. Asking these required reading the generated code.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: The git and general rules were in context, and the branch broadly follows them: commit subjects are lower case, under 50 characters and have no full stops, and the README lines break at full stops. Compliance is partial, though, because five commits use a `(vault)` scope (for example `chore(vault): prevent move`), which GIT_PRACTICE.md reserves for monorepos, and passs is not one.

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: The median is 53 generated lines per producing prompt across 14 producing prompts, which places the branch in band 2 (50 to 200); most prompts name a unit of work, but 'Ok, implement this' (233 lines), 'Both' (212 lines) and the vault CHANGELOG request (215 lines) each went past the 200-line reviewable limit.
